prompt: In normal adjustment of an astronomical telescope, the final image is formed:
options: At the focus of the eyepiece
explain: The intermediate image lies at fₑ of the eyepiece, so the final image is at infinity.
subject: Physics

prompt: The final image seen through an astronomical telescope is:
explain: Objective gives a real inverted image; the eyepiece magnifies it as a virtual image, still inverted.
subject: Physics

prompt: In normal adjustment, magnifying power of a telescope equals objective aperture divided by:
explain: The exit pupil (image of the objective) has diameter d = D/M, so M = D/d.
subject: Physics

prompt: For an astronomical telescope, the objective should have:
explain: Large fₒ gives large M; large aperture gives more light and better resolution. The eyepiece has small fₑ.
subject: Physics

prompt: Astronomical telescope: the intermediate image formed by the objective (object at infinity) lies at:
options: Focus of objective (at fₑ of eyepiece)
At the optical centre of eyepiece
At the near point of the eye
explain: Object at infinity gives the real image at Fₒ; in normal adjustment it coincides with the eyepiece focus.
subject: Physics

prompt: Image formed by a simple microscope (magnifier) is always:
explain: Object lies within focal length of a convex lens, so the image is virtual, erect and enlarged.
subject: Physics

prompt: For the final image at infinity (relaxed eye), the object is placed:
options: At the focus of the lens
At distance D from the lens
explain: Rays leave a point at F as a parallel beam, so the image forms at infinity: u = f.
subject: Physics

prompt: When the image is at the near point, M of a simple microscope equals:
explain: |v| = D, so M = D/|u| = |v/u|, the linear magnification.
subject: Physics

prompt: A simple microscope uses which lens for high magnifying power?
options: Convex lens of large focal length
Concave lens of small focal length
Convex lens of small focal length
Concave lens of large focal length
explain: M ∝ 1/f and only a converging lens gives a virtual magnified image, so use a convex lens of small f.
subject: Physics

prompt: White light passes obliquely through a glass slab. Lateral shift is largest for:
explain: Violet has the largest n, so it has the largest deviation (i−r) and hence the largest lateral shift.
subject: Physics

prompt: Glass slab (t, n_g) in water (n_w), viewed normally. Image shift of the object is:
explain: Replace 1 by the surrounding index: shift = t(1 − n_surr/n_slab).
subject: Physics

prompt: Two slabs (t₁,n₁) and (t₂,n₂) in air, viewed normally. Total image shift is:
explain: Normal shifts of the slabs add up independently.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a small angle of incidence i (radians) on a slab (t, n) in air, lateral shift ≈
explain: With sin(i−r) ≈ i−r, cos r ≈ 1 and r ≈ i/n, d ≈ t(i − i/n) = t·i(1 − 1/n).
subject: Physics

prompt: A fish sits at the centre of a thin spherical water bowl (n = 4/3). Seen from air, its image is magnified by:
explain: Image is at the same point (v = u), so m = n₁/n₂ = (4/3)/1 = 4/3.
subject: Physics

prompt: A point object at the first focus F₁ of a spherical refracting surface gives a refracted beam that is:
explain: Object at F₁ means the image is at infinity, so the emergent rays are parallel to the axis.
subject: Physics

prompt: For a convex air–glass surface, the focal length is smallest for which colour?
explain: Violet has the largest n, so n₂/(n₂−1) is smaller and f₂ is smaller.
subject: Physics

prompt: A concave surface facing the air, bounding glass (light going air → glass), has power that is:
explain: R < 0 and n₂ > n₁, so P < 0 and the surface is diverging.
subject: Physics

prompt: Ray falls normally on face 1 of prism (A, index n). It emerges from face 2 only if sin A is less than:
explain: Normal incidence gives r₂ = A. Emergence needs A < C, so sin A < sin C = 1/n.
subject: Physics

prompt: Angular dispersion between violet and red by a thin prism of small angle A is:
explain: δ = (n−1)A, so δ_v − δ_r = (n_v − n_r)A. Dividing by the mean deviation (n_y−1)A gives dispersive power.
subject: Physics

prompt: Moving from normal adjustment to image at near point, the telescope tube length:
explain: Eyepiece must be moved away from the objective: its object distance is fₑD/(D+fₑ)... see note: this is less than fₑ, so L = fₒ + uₑ decreases.
subject: Physics

prompt: In a Newtonian reflecting telescope, the secondary mirror is a:
explain: Newtonian design uses a small plane mirror at 45° to send the light to the side eyepiece.
subject: Physics

prompt: Angular magnification of a telescope is the ratio of angle subtended at the eye by:
options: Final image to that by object directly
Object to that by final image
Image to that by the objective's aperture
explain: M = β/α: angle subtended by the final image over angle subtended by the object at the unaided eye.
subject: Physics

prompt: Large astronomical telescopes use mirror objectives mainly because a mirror can be:
options: Supported over its whole back surface
Made with a shorter focal length only
Made to give an erect image
explain: Large mirrors are supported from behind and have no chromatic aberration; large lenses sag and are hard to make.
subject: Physics

prompt: The eye ring (exit pupil) of a telescope is the image of the:
options: Final image formed by the eye
Intermediate image formed by the eyepiece
explain: Eyepiece images the objective aperture; the eye is placed there to collect all the light.
subject: Physics

prompt: To raise the magnifying power of a given telescope in normal adjustment, replace the eyepiece with one of:
explain: M = fₒ/fₑ, so a smaller fₑ gives a larger M.
subject: Physics

prompt: A fish swims upward at speed v toward the surface of water (n). Its apparent speed seen from air (near-normal) is:
explain: Differentiating d_app = d/n with respect to time gives v_app = v/n.
subject: Physics

prompt: A glass slab in air is viewed normally. The image of an object behind it is shifted:
explain: The slab makes the object appear nearer to the observer by t(1 − 1/n).
subject: Physics

prompt: A point object is placed at the pole of a spherical refracting surface. Its image forms:
explain: With u = 0, the formula gives v = 0. The image coincides with the object at the pole.
subject: Physics

prompt: Newton's form for a lens (x₁, x₂ measured from the foci): the magnitude of transverse magnification is
explain: |m| = f/x₁ = x₂/f, where x₁ is the object's distance from the first focus.
subject: Physics

prompt: A slab is placed between a small object and the eye (near-normal view). The image shift depends on slab position as:
options: Larger if the slab is near the object
Larger if the slab is near the eye
Zero unless slab touches the object
explain: Shift = t(1 − 1/n) depends only on t and n, not on where the slab sits along the path.
subject: Physics

prompt: A coin under water is viewed from directly above. It appears shallowest in which colour of light?
explain: d_app = d/n and n is largest for violet, so the apparent depth is least for violet.
subject: Physics

prompt: A real object forms a real image through a single spherical refracting surface. The image is always:
options: erect or inverted, depending on n₁, n₂
explain: Real image has v > 0 and real object has u < 0, so m is negative for any n₁, n₂. The image is inverted.
subject: Physics

prompt: A real object moves along the axis of a thin lens. Its image moves:
options: Same direction as the object, always
Same direction only if image is real
Opposite only if image is virtual
explain: For a lens dv/dt = m²·du/dt with m² > 0, so both move the same way.
subject: Physics

prompt: A convex lens forms a real, inverted, magnified image. The object lies:
explain: For f < |u| < 2f the image is real, inverted, magnified and beyond 2F.
subject: Physics

prompt: A thin lens forms an image with m = +3. The image is:
explain: Positive m means erect, which for a real object means virtual; |m| = 3 > 1 means magnified.
subject: Physics

prompt: A real object is at distance |f| from a concave lens of focal length f. The magnification is:
explain: With f = −F and u = −F, m = f/(f+u) = −F/(−2F) = +1/2 (virtual, erect, diminished).
subject: Physics

prompt: An object moves along the axis of a lens or mirror at speed v. The image's axial speed, with magnification m, is:
explain: Differentiating the lens or mirror formula gives dv/dt = (v/u)² du/dt = m² du/dt.
subject: Physics

prompt: Light of refractive index n travels a distance d in a medium. Its optical path length is:
explain: Optical path is the equivalent distance in vacuum, equal to refractive index × geometric path (c·t = n·d).
subject: Physics

prompt: By Fermat's principle, light going between two points follows the path of:
explain: Fermat's principle: the actual path has extremum, usually minimum, travel time. Snell's law follows from it.

prompt: A ray goes from air through glass into water (parallel faces). Its angle in water depends on:
formula: n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂ = n₃ sinθ₃
options: Glass index and water index only
Air angle, glass index, water index
Air angle and water index only

prompt: Twinkling of stars is mainly caused by:
options: Dispersion of light by air molecules
Total internal reflection in the atmosphere

subject: Physics

prompt: Cauchy's relation n = A + B/λ² shows that refractive index of a transparent medium, with increasing λ:
explain: B is positive, so n falls as λ increases; blue has higher n than red.
subject: Physics

prompt: For fixed thickness and incidence angle, raising the slab's refractive index makes the lateral shift:
explain: Larger n gives smaller r, so (i − r) grows and the lateral shift increases, up to a limit of t.
subject: Physics

prompt: Marginal rays from a distant axial point meet a convex air–glass surface. They focus relative to paraxial rays:
options: On the other side of the pole
explain: Spherical aberration: rays far from the axis bend more and cross the axis closer to the surface.
subject: Physics

prompt: Parallel rays fall on a solid glass sphere (n = 1.5, radius R). They focus beyond the back surface at:
explain: First surface gives v = 3R. This is a virtual object R beyond the back surface, which then images at R/2.
subject: Physics

prompt: The power (n₂−n₁)/R of a single spherical refracting surface does NOT depend on:
explain: Power is set by the surface and the two media only, not by where the object is placed.
subject: Physics

prompt: Convex lens: object placed at the first principal focus F₁. The refracted rays are:
explain: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 0, so v = ∞. The image is at infinity and the emergent beam is parallel.
subject: Physics

prompt: A small object lies along the axis of a thin lens. Its longitudinal magnification is (m = transverse magnification):
explain: Differentiating 1/v − 1/u = 1/f gives dv/du = v²/u² = m². It is always positive, so the image is not inverted along the axis.
subject: Physics

prompt: The lens maker's formula is derived assuming:
options: Only a point object at infinity
explain: Lens thickness is neglected and rays are close to, and make small angles with, the axis.
subject: Physics

prompt: Thin lens (index nₗ) in a medium of index nₘ. Which expression gives 1/f?
explain: Replace n by the relative index nₗ/nₘ in the lens maker's formula.
subject: Physics

prompt: Which of the following does NOT change the focal length of a thin lens?
explain: f depends on n, R₁, R₂, wavelength and medium. It is independent of the object position.

prompt: A thin lens of index n₂ is in medium n₁ (n₂ > n₁). Its power P compared with that in air is:
explain: Relative index n₂/n₁ is less than n₂ (as n₁ > 1), so (n−1) falls and power decreases.
subject: Physics

prompt: The dimensional formula of the power of a lens is:
explain: P = 1/f, and f is a length, so P has dimension L⁻¹ (dioptre = m⁻¹).
subject: Physics

prompt: A thin meniscus shell has both surfaces of the same radius R, curved the same way. Its power is:
explain: R₁ = R₂ = R gives 1/R₁ − 1/R₂ = 0, so the power is zero.
subject: Physics

prompt: The power of a thin lens in a given medium does NOT depend on:
explain: Power is a property of the lens and its medium, not of where the object is placed.
subject: Physics

prompt: Four identical thin lenses, each of focal length 40 cm, are placed in contact. Combined power is:
explain: Each lens is +2.5 D, so four give +10 D (f = 10 cm).
subject: Physics

prompt: A plano-convex lens of power P is silvered on its plane face. It acts as a concave mirror of power:
explain: Light crosses the lens twice and the plane mirror adds no power, so P_eq = 2P.
subject: Physics

prompt: A convex lens and a concave lens of equal |f| are separated by a gap d. The system behaves as:
explain: P = P − P − d(P)(−P) = +dP² > 0, so the pair converges.
subject: Physics

prompt: Power of a thin lens (index μ_l) placed in a medium of index μ_m is:
explain: Replace μ by the relative index μ_l/μ_m in the lens maker's relation.
subject: Physics

prompt: Lenses of +2 D and −3 D are in contact. The combination is:
explain: P = 2 − 3 = −1 D, so it is concave with f = −1 m = −100 cm.
subject: Physics

prompt: Two thin lenses in contact are interchanged in order. The equivalent focal length:
explain: 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂ is symmetric in f₁ and f₂, so the order does not matter.
subject: Physics

prompt: A convex lens is cut along its axis. The halves have different n and are rejoined side by side. Images formed:
options: One image at the mean focal length
explain: Each half has its own focal length (different n), so an object gives two separate images.
